items.headline: Red tape, high cost: can Hong Kong’s new yacht scheme chart a smoother course?
items.detail: Retired harbour pilot Alex Yu Chi-leung sailed his 50-foot wooden yacht, Bowline, from Causeway Bay in Hong Kong to Dongao Island in Zhuhai under a new cross-border yachting scheme last week, but bureaucratic hurdles and shallow waters…

items.headline: China begins mining iron from tailings, low-grade ore that can meet its demand for decades
items.detail: China has launched a world-first industrial-scale facility to extract iron from previously discarded mine tailings and ultra-low-grade ore, turning waste into a valuable resource that can reduce its dependency on overseas supply.

items.headline: Signalling fault disrupts Hong Kong high-speed rail service, delaying 15 trains
items.detail: At least 15 high-speed cross-border train services were delayed after a signalling fault prompted a 45-minute disruption of northbound services in Hong Kong on Sunday morning.

items.headline: Junior Chinese customs officer killed in mudslide just 4 days into job deeply moves public
items.detail: The tragic death of a junior Chinese customs officer on the Sino-Nepal border, who had only been in her position for four days before being killed in a catastrophic mudslide, has stirred immense heartbreak online.

items.headline: Hired, then what? Malaysia’s deaf workers push past entry-level jobs
items.detail: Yap Yee Lin has been serving espresso at a Starbucks in Malaysia since 2012, longer than many of his colleagues have worked anywhere.
